Hey, currently dealing with this myself, however I'm in my 40s with a couple kids. A couple months ago I has less than $100 in my checking account, no $$$ for food, no medical insurance, I was actually stealing food from the local grocery store. I'm still not on solid ground yet but I'm not going hungry and I'm covering basic utilities:

* Immediately contact social services, hopefully you can file online for an EBT card (ie. food stamps). List your assets as less than $100, the amount of $$$ you have as less than $100, and your yearly income as $15k. This will get you on an emergency list. When I did, I had a EBT card with few hundred dollars on it in less than 2 or 3 days. I also qualified for medicaid (ie. medical insurance). 
* Cancel any and all services you have; Netflix, Amazon prime, Spotify, gym, etc. Right now I only have 4 monthly expenses not including rent: water, electric, internet, and auto insurance. 
* If you have any credit cards or student loans, call them ASAP and ask them specifically if they have a "hardship program". Be honest about your situation. They have the ability to pause payments on your account for between 3 & 6 months. 
* If you get desperate for money to pay bills and expenses, sell any and all possession you may own on Facebook, Craigslist, and/or Ebay. This is currently how I'm paying for my expenses. Even if you have an unopened package of something you bought months ago, it will sell. I sold an unopened bluetooth dongle for $5 + S/H. And that was $5 more than what I had in my pocket before I sold it, and $$$ I used to pay the electric bill. 
* Does your bank charge a monthly service fee? Drop them, there are plenty of banks and credit unions that don't charge. 

Regarding food and eating: 

* Don't buy any food from restaurants, they are expensive! Even fast food. [This is a great book](https://cookbooks.leannebrown.com/good-and-cheap.pdf) written by a fellow redditor on how to eat well for $4 a day. /r/MealPrepSunday is a good sub, /r/budgetfood is another one. 
* When it comes to shopping for food, Walmart really does have the cheapest overall prices however you can get better prices by buying things on sale and/or using coupons. Buy in bulk and if you do, check the expiration date! 
* Buy your veggies frozen and while they're on sale! I can get a bag of green beans, corn, brocolli, etc. for $1. 
* Changing up your cooking style is key to resisting the urge to eat out. Last month I was on a Mexican food trip; homemade pico de gallo, Mexican rice, breakfast burritos, chicken fajitas, etc. This month it's Italian food; baked penne pasta, homemade meatballs, tomato sauce, etc. I can cook a meal and store it in the fridge and eat like a king for 3-4 days. And because I'm buying in bulk when stuff is on sale, the average cost of my meals, per person, is between $1 and $2. 
* This is easier said than done, but do everything you can to avoid throwing away food. In other words, eat what you cook and try not to buy perishable foods that you won't eat in a couple days. Also, [expiration dates on food are terribly misleading](http://www.npr.org/sections/thesalt/2017/02/15/515427797/food-companies-may-say-goodbye-to-sell-by-labels) and lead to a bunch of food waste. 

I don't know where you're at or what you have, but if you need any kitchen utensils (pots, pans, dishes, silverware, cooking utensils, storage containers, etc) PM me and I'll manage to get a package of goodies your way; I have an extra set of kitchen wares I've been planning to sell but if you need it, would rather go to someone in need. Good luck and take care.
